To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of caffeic phenethyl ester, a naturally occurring antioxidant, and melatonin, an antioxidant hormone, on age‐related cardiac and vascular damage in rats are similar and that these compounds are effective in reducing the age‐related oxidative stress.

the administration of CAPE (50 mg/kg) and melatonin (50 mg/ kg) significantly decreased the oxidative stress in the heart and the thoracic aorta in aged rats, and also prevented the development of the age‐related histopathological alterations in the heart and in the thoracic aortas.
melatonin and caffeic acid phenylethyl ester (CAPE), which are both antioxidants, are efficient in preventing age‐related oxidative stress and cardiovascular remodeling in the heart and the aorta.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of melatonin and CAPe on age‐related oxidative stress and vascular remodeling in the cardiovascular system of rats.
the effects of CAPE and/or melatonin on age-related vascular remodeling and cardiac tissue injury.
the effects of melatonin and CApe on the age‐related oxidative stress‐induced cardiovascular damage in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
melatonin and CApe are beneficial in preventing and reducing age‐related oxidative stress and cellular damage.
melatonin and CAPe have beneficial effects in preventing age‐related oxidative stress and cellular damage in cardiovascular tissues.
melatonin and CAPe are beneficial in delaying age-related cardiovascular damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antioxidant effect of melatonin and CApe is more prominent in the thoracic aorta than in the heart of aged rats.
melatonin is a powerful antioxidant and free radical scavenger and CAPE is also an effective antioxidant.
CAPE and melatonin are effective in delaying the aging process by reducing oxidative stress and improving the antioxidant system status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CAPE is a potent antioxidant and anti‐inflammatory agent and may be useful for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases.
CAPE and melatonine may be used as a potential means of preventing age‐related oxidative stress and cardiovascular damage.
the antioxidant intervention studies with melatonin and CAFE may be a useful strategy for preventing age‐related vascular alterations.
